method: Coordinator web_fetch of actual public dictionary pages; relevant complete headings inspected alongside frozen JMdict packets. A returned heading is not verification of other entries on the same page.

entries.heading: もも【桃】
entries.evidence: Sense1 names the deciduous peach tree and edible fruit; sense2 abbreviates 桃色; sense3 names a cotton boll; sense4 is a historical layered-colour combination; sense5 is a crest. The page also returned 字通 トウ/もも and phonetic analysis, but that analysis is not needed for the planned modern-shape mnemonic.
entries.disposition: Teach peach tree/fruit and a brief pink-abbreviation recognition note; directly guard existing ピンク in the word quiz. Cotton-boll, historical costume and crest senses are recorded as inspected, not developed into invented ordinary examples.
entries.limits: 6000-character return stops in the later 字通 compound list, not in the complete Daijisen heading. No full-page or every-dictionary claim.

entries.heading: はく‐とう【白桃】; しろ‐もも【白桃】; 白桃 はくとう
entries.evidence: はくとう sense1 concerns a white-flowered peach, sense2 the fruit cultivar with white flesh and some reddish skin colouring. The separate しろもも heading distinguishes the ornamental white-flowered peach from the fruit cultivar and also gives a yamamomo cultivar sense. Nipponica confirms a peach cultivar and white skin/flesh.
entries.disposition: Use the frozen JMdict はくとう/white-peach family for the linked on-reading example; qualify cultivar naming and do not claim that every occurrence has one reading or every fruit has unmarked white skin. No invented しろもも allocation to the on reading.
entries.limits: Digital Daijisen heading is empty in this extraction and supplies no definition. Seisenban says discovery1901 whereas Nipponica says1899; leave that unnecessary chronology out of teaching rather than adjudicating it.

entries.heading: しょう‐ちく‐ばい【松竹梅】
entries.evidence: Noun1(1) names the auspicious pine/bamboo/ume grouping used in pictures and celebrations; noun1(2) names labels replacing three grades. Later entries discuss musical titles and a sake brand, not unrestricted synonyms of the grouping or a botanical origin for the characters.
entries.disposition: Teach the grouping and conventional high/middle/low labels supported by the exact frozen JMdict family and existing 松/竹/梅 articles. No historical chronology, universal price guarantee or claim that all uses denote a menu.
entries.limits: Digital Daijisen heading is empty. Fetch stops in later unrelated mention excerpts after the relevant complete Seisenban heading; not a full-page certification.

limits: Evidence supports exact bounded claims, not frequency, exhaustive senses, example naturalness certification, native-speaker review or publication. Complete frozen JMdict families remain the primary spelling/reading/restriction evidence.
